bull.b: High and growing subscription mix (55% of revenue) with 14% organic subscription growth and ~111% net revenue retention improves predictability and upsell economics. Durable recurring revenue reduces churn risk and supports stable cash flow and multiyear customer lifetime value.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and de-levered balance sheet
bull.b: Substantial FCF and a dramatic reduction in gross/net debt materially strengthen financial flexibility. Low leverage and sizable equity provide runway for reinvestment, product development, and M&A while reducing solvency risk through economic cycles, a durable cushion for execution.

bull.t: AI-driven product traction and scale advantage
bull.b: Rapid AI adoption embedded across products creates differentiated automation and measurable ROI for clients, raising switching costs. Combined with large transaction volume and payer/provider integrations, AI + data network effects reinforce a structural competitive moat and higher deal sizes.

bear.t: Elevated implementation backlog & long deal ramps
bear.b: Large, multi-module contracts lengthen time between booking and revenue recognition, making growth lumpy and extending payback periods. Persistent backlog pressures professional services capacity and execution, raising the risk that strong bookings do not translate quickly into sustained revenue.

A meaningful portion of revenue is tied to patient payment volumes which are shifting structurally (print-to-digital) and are exposed to seasonality and utilization. This mix risk can mute topline predictability and requires product adaptation to preserve transaction-driven revenue streams long term.

bear.t: Historic margin volatility and modest ROE
bear.b: Although profitability turned positive, historical swings in operating margins and only modest return on equity indicate execution and capital efficiency are not yet consistent. Sustaining margins as the company scales will be critical to convert growth into durable shareholder returns.
